name: Env reflector
purpose: Regenerates a `.env` file at the repo root from the current manifest slice and the vendor-resolved values, for the local developer tools that expect one. Runs on demand; overwrites atomically; never treats the resulting `.env` as authoritative.
responsibilities: Accept `--deployable <id>` and `--env <env>`; resolve the slice through TAC-902 and the values through TAC-901 (AC-8106-1).
Write the `.env` atomically: write to a temp file in the same directory and rename over the target so a partial write is never observable to a concurrent reader (AC-8106-1).
Refuse to run when the target `.env` path is not gitignored at the repo root; emit `SECRETS_DOTENV_NOT_IGNORED` naming the path (defence against a project that mis-configures `.gitignore`).
Never emit secret values to any surface other than the resulting file bytes; the command's own stdout, stderr, and audit event carry names and counts only.

Support per-environment reflection variants (`.env.dev`, `.env.ci`, `.env.live`) selected by the `--env` flag; when the same command is re-run with a different `--env` the previously-written variant is left untouched.
internalStructure: One stateless command handler. Composes the manifest loader (TAC-902), the Secrets Manager client (TAC-901), and a small `writeAtomic` utility. The output shape is a POSIX-style `KEY=value` file with values escaped for values containing whitespace, quotes, or newlines.

interfaces.name: fileSystem
interfaces.description: Project-supplied file reader-writer supporting temp-file creation and atomic rename.

interfaces.name: gitignoreCheck
interfaces.description: Project-supplied predicate answering whether a given path is gitignored (usually a shell-out to `git check-ignore`).

dependencies.name: Secrets Manager client
dependencies.description: Source of the resolved values for the target slice.

tradeoffs: The reflector puts secret material on disk in a file most tooling has read access to. That trade is the cost of interoperability with the tools that expect a `.env`; the atomic-write plus gitignore-required-check plus explicit re-run posture keeps the reflection legible as ephemeral rather than authoritative. Projects that prefer never to touch disk (in-memory-only container starts) skip the reflector and let their tooling read from the client directly.
